page.layout: Full-width title block at the top, in large capitals: "PER QVAM ILLVSTRIS, ET FILI INSTAR DILECTISSIMÆ IN DOMINO." Below it one text column with a large woodcut initial S at the start of the first paragraph. No margin notes. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.l: PER QVAM ILLV-
STRIS, ET FILI IN-
STAR DILECTISSIMÆ IN DOMINO.
SPIÆ[?] deuotissimi quondam
patris tui animæ renunciaretur
de relictis abs te studiis, &
spretâ gubernatione mea; cer-
tè tui huius instituti rationem
vbicunq; etiám locorum dege-
ret, quàm maximè essetimprobatura. Siquidem
vltrà modum amans te pater, & salutis
tuæ cupidus, quum neq; meliori præsidio, neq;
tutelæ magis securæ, quàm nostræ, committi te
posse intelligeret; ab ipsis mox incunabulis, &
vixdum etiam pedibus recta incedentem ad
Ecclesiam & Collegium nostrum adduxit: vbi
te omnibus Patribus cognoscendum exhi-
bens, singulatim commendauit. Et quia tunc
ego præter reliquos omnes, indolis tuæ viuaci-
tate, & forma huic conueniente captus me illi
obtuli, vt tui curam haberem, teq; erudiendo
instituerem: ille, cum primis se fortunatum
inde prædicans, palàm confessus est, sibi in hac
vita nihil isto iucundius accidisse. Ac quoniam

page.notes: Woodcut initial S with the following word "PIÆ" in capitals: the reading "SPIÆ" is uncertain; the first letters beside the initial are hard to make out. The top of the first column shows faint ghosting of ornament and text below the title (show-through, not transcribed). A small stray mark "/" lies at the lower left, not transcribed. Printed spellings kept as they appear: "essetimprobatura" (space missing in print), "accidisse". The word "renunciaretur" is partly obscured on the scan. Heading, last line and catchword "aduersa" are read from the scan with moderate confidence.
